comments:
The "btsun pa grags pa rgyal mtshan" who wrote down (ID:4794) could be Ze'u grags pa rgyal mtshan/Chu mig pa grags pa rgyal mtshan (ID:6133), a teacher of sKyo ston. (See Skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims kyi rnam thar in [LRSRMBWG]: 349a2). 
According to [NTGHCZA8]: 65, n. 145, this Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan could be the "Grags rgyal" mentioned in Sangs rgyas sgom pa's biography. In fact this “slob dpon Grags rgyal” bestowed on Sangs rgyas sgom pa (1179-1250) similar teachings to those that we find listed as passed from Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan to sKyo ston. The gDams ngag mdzod reports a Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan in the transmission of the white Jambhala (dzam dkar) that runs thus: spyan ras gzigs| rgya brtson 'gris seng ge| nag tsho tshul rgyal| rong pa phyag sor ba| pu to ba| sha ra ba| gtum ston pa| chu mig pa grags pa rgyal mtshan| gro ston bdud rtsi grags| zhang ston chos blo| mchims nam mkha' grags […] (the list reaches Tāranātha and then refers to a lineage given previously for the following lineage holders, so it would seem that the source for this lineage is given somewhere in Tāranātha's writings). If this is the case, this Chu mig pa Grags pa rgyal mtshan would be already a student of the first abbot of sNar thang gTum ston grags pa (1106-1166). This would be possible only if this Grags pa rgyal mtshan was born around the late 1150s and taught sKyo ston when he was already about 70 years of age.
